definitions.explanation: The scientific study of crime, its causes, consequences, and prevention.

examples.japanese: {犯罪学|はんざいがく}を{専攻|せんこう}する。
{犯罪学|はんざいがく}の{観点|かんてん}から{分析|ぶんせき}する。
examples.english: To analyze from a criminological perspective.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{犯罪学|はんざいがく}の{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}として、{再犯|さいはん}{防止|ぼうし}プログラムの{開発|かいはつ}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: As a criminology researcher, he is working on developing recidivism prevention programs.

notes:
A compound of {犯罪|はんざい} (crime) and {学|がく} (study, science). An interdisciplinary field that draws on sociology, psychology, and law to understand criminal behavior and inform crime prevention policy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犯罪学|はんざいがく}の{研究|けんきゅう}: criminology research
- {犯罪学|はんざいがく}{者|しゃ}: criminologist
- {犯罪学|はんざいがく}の{理論|りろん}: criminological theory
- {犯罪学|はんざいがく}{的|てき}: criminological

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {刑事学|けいじがく}: criminal science — focuses on the legal and investigative aspects of crime
- {犯罪|はんざい}{心理学|しんりがく}: criminal psychology — the psychological study of criminal behavior
- {法学|ほうがく}: law; jurisprudence — the broader study of law and legal systems
